items.note:
This page uses secondary analysis of the same Penguin public data to arrange four relative time points. The three-month rhythm is a course example, not an institutional requirement or completed activity. Four complete Markdown drafts and CSV/JSON are arranged in outreach-packet. The first week explains the 146 records with 73 males and 73 males each, and the mean difference is 4.62 mm; the end of the first month explains the screening and code version from 344 to 152 to 146; the end of the second month uses preset questions and answers to explain the unmeasured swimming speed, distribution overlap and extrapolation limitations; the end of the third month checks the consistency of the link, hash and recalculation, and retains the old version and reasons if modification is needed. The Q&A is set by the course and cannot be said to reflect the reader feedback received. There is no platform publishing, calendar reminders, access or adoption of data. The distinction between on-site Q&A and feedback on the original page 10 is retained in the R3 and R4 drafts: answers return to the tested content, and real evidence is left for dissemination statistics, specific questions and subsequent use. Formal dissemination requires the author to confirm the material, signature, version and public permission; unconfirmed findings will not be added to the update frequency. The next section turns to the actual operating scope of local and cloud Agents. After the first quarter is over, the next quarter will be planned based on actual problems, data and available energy; updates can also be paused when there are no data changes, and there is no automatic release cycle.
